decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark — paste a web address”; Round 1 client approves the proposed v1.
decisions.note: The specification-gate decision supports saving a bookmark by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits automatic collection to “page title or the address itself” and asks about “favicons” and “notes/descriptions” as missing possibilities; client says only to keep “best-effort page-title fetching.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, automatic metadata collection omits description, favicon, and preview image. The client preserves title fetching but does not express the missing reference metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers an “optional custom title” and later title editing but presents descriptions as potentially missing; Round 1 client approves as-is.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, title editing is covered, but the required editable auto-collected description is absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Edit & delete — fix a title/address”; notes and descriptions are listed as possibly missing. Round 1 client approves as-is.
decisions.note: The presented edit scope omits description and note, so it does not provide all required editable bookmark fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes removing bookmarks “with a confirmation step”; Round 1 client approves.
decisions.note: The specification includes permanent bookmark deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker describes only seeing saved bookmarks “in a list” and identifies “favicons” and “notes/descriptions” as missing possibilities; client approves as-is.
decisions.note: The specification-gate list lacks the required description and favicon presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “click to open the original page in a new tab”; Round 1 client approves.
decisions.note: Selecting the presented bookmark opens its original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers: “Tags & search (P3) — keep in scope, or trim v1”; Round 1 client selects: “Please keep tags, search … in v1.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the offered trim alternative would omit tagging and tag filtering; the client selects the reference-conforming inclusion alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker defines keyword search only “across title/address/tags”; Round 1 client asks to keep search but does not mention description or note search.
decisions.note: The proposed searchable fields omit description and note. Keeping the already-described search does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker mentions “duplicate-address warnings”; Round 1 client approves without clarifying whether the warning guides the user to edit the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the record does not establish whether duplicate handling conforms to edit-existing guidance or merely warns/rejects.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker specifies “most-recent-first ordering”; Round 1 client approves as-is.
decisions.note: The specification fixes one ordering and presents no user-selectable sort key.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker asks whether anything is missing, including “notes/descriptions”; Round 1 client approves without requesting notes.
decisions.note: The specification explicitly leaves bookmark notes outside the presented model and therefore lacks markdown note writing/rendering.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope table: “Import/export of existing browser bookmarks — out”; Round 1 client: “Approve as-is.”
decisions.note: Import and export are explicitly excluded. Bare approval does not establish that the client noticed or accepted the reference difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker plans a create-bookmark API and URL validation; Round 2 client approves the plan.
decisions.note: The plan retains URL-based bookmark creation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Page titles — Fetched best-effort on save … falls back to the address”; the data summary contains only URL, title, and timestamps. Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: At the plan gate, automatic enrichment remains limited to title and omits description, favicon, and preview image.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker’s model is “Bookmark (url, title, timestamps)” with inline editing; Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: The plan supports title editing but contains no editable description before or after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents inline editing for a model containing “url, title, timestamps” and tags; Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: The planned edit operation lacks description and note fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker plans “delete-with-confirmation”; Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: The plan retains permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker plans “a bookmark list,” while its bookmark model is only “url, title, timestamps” plus tags; Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: The planned list cannot expose the required description and favicon because those fields are absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specifies Bookmark-to-Tag many-to-many data and create/edit bookmark APIs; Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: The plan supports assigning multiple tags to bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker plans “tag filter chips” and tag filtering in the list endpoint; Round 2 client approves.
decisions.note: Selecting a tag filter is provided.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker plans keyword search with a model limited to URL/title/tags; Round 2 client approves “simple substring search.”
decisions.note: The plan omits full-text matching over description and note. The client does not state that those fields are expected.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly selects “Plain substring search”; Round 2 client says “simple substring search … suitable.”
decisions.note: Plain substring search lacks #tag syntax, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, and exact quoted phrases. The client names the chosen search style but does not identify any of these expected capabilities or their absence, so this is not accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says URL normalization enables “reliable duplicate detection”; Round 2 client approves without clarifying the resulting duplicate-save behavior.
decisions.note: At the plan gate, detection is specified but whether it guides editing, rejects, or otherwise handles the duplicate remains indeterminate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker’s US1 test is “Save a URL”; Round 3 client requests implementation.
decisions.note: The task breakdown preserves URL-based saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker describes saving as “de-duped”; Round 3 client requests the full v1 without clarifying whether duplicate saves lead to editing the existing item.
decisions.note: At the task gate, “de-duped” establishes duplicate prevention but not the required edit-existing guidance.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker’s US2 task outcome is “List newest-first”; Round 3 client requests implementation without asking for selectable sorting.
decisions.note: The task breakdown continues a fixed sort rather than user-selectable sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “titles open in new tab”; Round 3 client requests implementation.
decisions.note: The task breakdown opens the original bookmark target.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “delete needs confirm, stays gone”; Round 3 client requests implementation.
decisions.note: The task breakdown includes permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker’s US4 independent test includes “Tag filter”; Round 3 client requests implementation.
decisions.note: The task breakdown includes filtering by a selected tag.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker carries the approved plan into US4 as “keyword search”; Round 3 client asks for all four stories without changing its search behavior.
decisions.note: At the task gate, the limited URL/title/tag substring search remains in force, omitting required fields and advanced query syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker offers implementation of the suggested US1+US2 MVP or “all” of full v1; Round 3 client selects: “full v1, including all four user stories.”
decisions.note: At the implementation-scope choice, the client selects the alternative that includes the fully conforming delete, tag-assignment, and tag-filter features. Edit and search are excluded from this captured decision because their offered specifications still diverge in other respects.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports US1 Save with HTTP/HTTPS URL validation and persistence; Round 4 client accepts the app.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation supports saving by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports only “best-effort page-title fetch with fallback”; Round 4 client says the app matches the approved behavior.
decisions.note: At implementation review, automatic metadata still omits description, favicon, and preview image. General approval does not surface those differences.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says the app follows the approved URL/title data plan and provides inline editing; Round 4 client accepts it.
decisions.note: The implemented presentation retains editable titles but no editable auto-collected description.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports “inline edit” under the previously presented URL/title/tag model; Round 4 client accepts the app.
decisions.note: At implementation review, bookmark editing still lacks description and note.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports “delete-with-confirmation, changes persist”; Round 4 client accepts.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion is implemented.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker explicitly reports “duplicate rejection”; Round 4 client generally accepts the completed app.
decisions.note: At implementation review, a duplicate save is rejected rather than guiding the user to edit the existing bookmark. The client does not state the expected edit-existing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports a “newest-first list” with titles and tags under the URL/title/tag model; Round 4 client accepts.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation lacks per-item description and favicon, so the required readability-first item content is incomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “titles open in a new tab”; Round 4 client accepts.
decisions.note: Selecting the presented title navigates to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker invites the client to “tag it” and reports delivered tag functionality; Round 4 client accepts.
decisions.note: Bookmark tagging is implemented.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports “tag filter chips” and invites the client to “search/filter it”; Round 4 client accepts.
decisions.note: Filtering by a selected tag is implemented.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports “keyword search across title/address/tags”; Round 4 client generally accepts all four stories.
decisions.note: The implementation search omits description and note. The client does not express those expected fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker says the implementation follows “exactly the approved plan,” whose search decision was plain substring search; Round 4 client accepts it.
decisions.note: At implementation review, #tag queries, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, and exact quoted phrases remain absent and are not surfaced by the response.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reports only a “newest-first list”; Round 4 client accepts the app.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation retains a fixed ordering with no user-selectable sort key.
